name: Dockmaster Deepwade Boot
description: A hulking, knee-high waterproof boot built for the loading docks along Lake Michigan's industrial edge. Thick vulcanized rubber shell, sealed seams, and a non-slip tread pattern designed to grip wet steel grating. Comes in a uniform dark grey with a faded orange reflective stripe around the ankle that loses most of its brightness within a season. Ugly by any standard, but a dockworker's feet stay dry.
functionality: Waterproof to 2m submersion, oil-resistant sole, basic ankle brace support
what_it_says: You work the docks or the flood-prone lower Shelf. You don't care about looks — you care about keeping your feet.
story_hooks: A pair left behind at a crime scene — the distinctive tread pattern is traceable to a specific dock shift rotation.
The cork insoles are a known hiding spot for small contraband among long-haul dock crews.
